cohort: 110 pregnant women with thrombocytopenia at a tertiary care center
finding: Gestational thrombocytopenia was the most common etiology of thrombocytopenia in pregnancy, and maternal and fetal outcomes were generally good with strict vigilance during intrapartum and postpartum periods.
mod_finding: The majority of women with thrombocytopenia (41.8%) underwent spontaneous vaginal delivery.
